newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FOCUS-Manila shares up again but GNP may hold key.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Manila shares up again but GNP may hold key.

text.p: Philippines shares swung upwards for the second straight day on Tuesday but analysts said it was too early to say if the bad times were over even thought latest news on the economy has been encouraging.
The main index, in a spill-over from Monday's buying exuberance and helped by an overnight jump of the Dow Jones, rose 1.47 percent to settle at 2,776.53 points.
Analysts said the market was still in a consolidation phase and its direction could depend on the first quarter gross national figure (GNP) figure expected to be released at the end of the month.
"The continuity of this rebound will be determined by the release of first quarter economic figures," Citicorp Securities research head Fiona Paua said.

Some traders said they believed the market had already taken into account unofficial reports that first quarter GNP would be lower than expected and that sentiment would depend on how much lower it would be.
The market, however, has taken heart from this week's news of lower inflation in April and a sharp rise in exports in March.

But Wilfred Son Keng Po, managing director at Angping and Associates Securities, said the market was still waiting for more positive economic news and it was premature to say if it could sustain the two-day upturn.

Blue chips were among the day's top gainers. Metropolitan Bank and Trust Co closed 10 pesos higher at 600 pesos, Manila Electric Company B gained six pesos to settle at 138 pesos and Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co posted a 45-peso rise to close at 780 pesos.
The bourse's newest star, movie producer Premiere Entertaimnment Productions, gained two centavos and settled at 1.28 pesos. Its share price has risen 28 percent since its listing on Monday.
Turnover was a billion pesos shy of Monday's but still a substantial 3.02 billion with 81 gainers and 57 losers while 63 issues were unchanged.
